key_insight: Conditional Flow Matching can generate physically plausible 3D instantaneous urban wind and temperature fields from building geometry and mean flow, capturing turbulent variability rather than only deterministic averages.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast LES-like microclimate prediction for iterative urban design, improving feasibility for turbulence-aware planning and climate adaptation.
method: Condition the generator on building geometry and mean flow fields.
Use Conditional Flow Matching to sample full 3D instantaneous velocity and temperature fields.
Generate in overlapping pixel-space blocks with shared-noise initialization to reduce GPU memory use and preserve continuity.
evidence_signal: Compared with LES reference data, the surrogate reported low NRMSE for first-order statistics (2.99% wind, 1.77% temperature) and strong agreement on second-order turbulence metrics, TKE, PDFs, and vertical profiles.
watch_item: The overlapping pixel-space generation strategy may be sensitive to domain tiling and continuity settings, so deployment should verify boundary consistency and generalization across unseen urban morphologies.
paper_title: Conditional Flow Matching for Generation of 3D Multi-variable Instantaneous Urban Microclimate Fields
